land.text: the four enclaves of Pondichéry, Yanam, Mahé and Karikal (de facto 1 November 1954) and Chandernagore (de facto 2 May 1950, merged with West Bengal 2 October 1954)

Chandernagore left earlier (2 May 1950 de facto, per the Chandannagar page).

capitals.name: Pondichéry (Puducherry)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Pondichéry'. The French held the town through four British occupations (1761-65, 1778-83, 1793-1802, 1803-16) and a Dutch one (1693-99); the governors' seat returned each time. The page also shows a Government House at Chandernagore (c. 1850) but names no capital move.

correction.text: Pondichéry only: 'On 4 February 1673, Bellanger de l'Espinay, a French officer, took up residence in the Danish Lodge in Pondichéry'; the page dates no other French holding in India for 1673-1691 (Surat 1668 and Masulipatam 1669 were factories, lost by 1720)

keyframe_review.note: 1673-1676, 3,703 km2 = 10 cells: 9 on Réunion and 1 in India at Chandernagore, which the page founds in 1692, not 1673. Not French India. The infobox gives 510 km2 for 1936 (the text attributes it to 1950); five res-5 cells already total about 1,260 km2, so the correction is one cell (Pondichéry) by the grid's granularity.

The French India page lists no Madagascar, Comoros or Mascarene establishment, and the French East India Company page (read for this) dates no territory at all, so those 45 cells are not French India on any page opened; they are Cliopatria's lumping of French Indian-Ocean holdings under this Name. The 5 Mauritius cells run 1721-1814; the Treaty of Paris (1814) page confirms only that Mauritius was 'handed over to British control' in 1814.

keyframe_review.note: 1727-1740, 10,094 km2 = 20 cells: 9 Réunion, 5 Mauritius, 2 Comoros, 4 India (Pondichéry, Chandernagore, Yanam, Mahé). The four Indian cells agree with the page's dates (Yanam 1723, Mahé 1725); the other 16 cells are not French India.

The four enclaves follow on 1 November 1954 (de facto), 1962 (de jure).

region.text: Pondichéry, where the French officer Bellanger de l'Espinay settled in the Danish Lodge

ledger.note: 1673: the French settle at Pondichéry. 'On 4 February 1673, Bellanger de l'Espinay, a French officer, took up residence in the Danish Lodge in Pondichéry'; the page adds that the French acquired the area in 1673 but names neither the seller nor a boundary, so the region is the town's cell (my reading). Earlier French factories: Surat (1668) and Masulipatam (1669), both lost by 1720 per the page; they are not drawn.

region.text: Chandernagore on the Hooghly, with the Nawab's permission

ledger.note: 1692: the French found Chandernagore. 'Chandernagore was established in 1692, with the permission of Nawab Shaista Khan' (French India page). The Chandannagar page disagrees: Boureau-Deslandes 'paid 40,000 coins to the Mughal subahdar in 1688 to gain control of the area and build a factory', and the infobox dates the French colony to 1696 (Fort d'Orléans built 1696-97). The counterpart is read as the Mughal Empire because Shaista Khan was the Mughal governor of Bengal (my reading; neither page says 'Mughal' for him).

1693: the Dutch take Pondichéry. 'In 1693, the Dutch captured Pondichéry and augmented the fortifications.' The Dutch Republic's Indian possessions were the Company's; the Cliopatria neighbour list gives dutch-republic as the touching shape.
1699: the French recover Pondichéry. 'The French regained the town in 1699 through the Treaty of Ryswick, signed on 20 September 1697' (the page gives both years; the town changed hands in 1699).

1723: the French acquire Yanam. The page lists 'Yanam: 1723 (peaceful acquisition)'; it names neither the ruler nor the terms, so the counterpart is unnamed. A gap-filler should open the Yanam article.
1725: the French acquire Mahé. The page lists 'Mahé: 1725' and gives neither the ruler nor the terms.

1739: the French acquire Karikal. The page lists 'Karaikal: 1739' and gives neither the ruler nor the terms; the Cliopatria neighbour list has thanjavur-maratha-kingdom touching French India from 1741, which is a hint, not a source.

21 September 1746: the French take Madras. 'On 21 September 1746, the French captured the British outpost at Madras.' The East India Company has no dossier; the Cliopatria British Colonial Empire row touches French India 1709-1756.
1748: Madras goes back. 'In the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748), Madras was given back to the British in exchange for the French fortress of Louisbourg in North America.'

23 March 1757: Clive and Watson take Chandernagore. The Chandannagar page: Clive and Watson 'bombarded and captured Chandannagar on 23 March 1757'; the Carnatic Wars page: 'British forces captured the French settlement of Chandernagore in 1757'.

15 January 1761: Pondichéry falls to the British. 'First British occupation, 15 Jan 1761 - 25 June 1765'; 'In 1761, the British razed Pondichéry to the ground.' The Carnatic Wars page: 'After Wandiwash, Pondicherry fell to the British in 1761.' The page does not say whether Karikal, Mahé and Yanam fell in the same war.

1763: Chandernagore is restored. 'Chandannagore was restored to the French in 1763.' The Carnatic Wars page: the Treaty of Paris (1763) 'returned Chandernagore and Pondicherry to France, and allowed the French to have trading posts in India' and 'forbade French traders from administering them'.
25 June 1765: Pondichéry is handed back. 'In 1765, Pondichéry was returned to France in accordance with a 1763 peace treaty.'
1778: the second British occupation of Pondichéry begins (1778-1783, ended by the Treaty of Paris (1783)); the page gives no month.
1783: the Treaty of Paris (1783) ends the second British occupation of Pondichéry.
23 August 1793: the third British occupation of Pondichéry begins (to 18 June 1802).
1794: the British retake Chandernagore, 'retaken by the British in 1794 in the Napoleonic Wars'. The page does not mention the Treaty of Amiens (1802) interval or a second capture in 1803.
18 June 1802: the Treaty of Amiens ends the third British occupation of Pondichéry.
August 1803: the fourth British occupation of Pondichéry begins (to 26 September 1816).
1816: Chandernagore returns to France. 'The city was returned to France in 1816'; the 1816 enclave is 'a 3 sq mi (7.8 km2) enclave of surrounding territory'.

region.text: Pondichéry, with Karikal, Mahé and Yanam

ledger.note: 26 September 1816: Pondichéry is handed back after the Treaty of Paris (1814). 'The five establishments and lodges were returned to France after the Napoleonic Wars' (1816). The Treaty of Paris (1814) page is silent on India (it dates the signing 30 May 1814 and names the Mauritius, Seychelles, Tobago and Saint Lucia exceptions).

2 May 1950: Chandernagore passes to India de facto. 'The French allowed the Indian government to assume de facto control over Chandannagar' after the 19 June 1949 referendum (98.5% for joining India); the page gives 2 February 1951 for the formal cession, 9 June 1952 for the de jure transfer and 2 October 1954 for merger into West Bengal (its infobox labels 2 February 1951 'de facto', which disagrees with its body). The French India page also gives 2 May 1950 for the cession.

1 November 1954: the four enclaves pass to India. 'On 1 Nov 1954, the four enclaves of Pondichéry, Yanam, Mahe and Karikal were de facto transferred to the Indian Union' (Kizhoor referendum; first High Commissioner appointed 21 October 1954). The de jure union came in 1962. The lodges at Machilipatnam, Kozhikode and Surat were ceded on 6 October 1947 (not drawn).
1954: French India ends. De facto transfer of the last four enclaves on 1 November 1954; 'The de jure union of French India with India did not take place until 1962.'

wars.name: Dutch occupation of Pondichéry (Nine Years' War)
wars.outcome: The Dutch captured Pondichéry in 1693 and strengthened its fortifications; the French regained it in 1699 under the Treaty of Ryswick (signed 20 September 1697).
wars.note: The page does not name the war; the Nine Years' War is the war the Treaty of Ryswick ended (not stated on the page).

wars.name: Carnatic Wars
wars.outcome: The French took Madras in 1746 and gave it back in 1748; the British took Chandernagore in 1757 and Pondichéry in 1761; the Treaty of Paris (1763) returned Chandernagore and Pondicherry to France (Pondichéry in 1765) without the right to administer them.
wars.note: The page's infobox span is 1744-1763 while its text says the first wars ran 1740-1748; the Second War's start is undated and ends with the Treaty of Pondicherry (1754). The page does not mention Dupleix's or Bussy's territorial grants or the Northern Circars, so no French gain of 1749-1754 is in the ledger.

wars.name: American Revolutionary War (Indian theatre)
wars.outcome: Second British occupation of Pondichéry, 1778-1783, ended by the Treaty of Paris (1783).
wars.note: The page does not name the war; it gives the occupation years and the 1783 treaty only.

wars.name: French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars (Indian theatre)
wars.outcome: Third British occupation of Pondichéry 23 August 1793 - 18 June 1802 (Treaty of Amiens); fourth August 1803 - 26 September 1816 (Treaty of Paris, 1814); Chandernagore retaken in 1794 and returned in 1816.
wars.note: Chandernagore dates from the Chandannagar page (1794, 1816).

certainty.note: Factory and village grants whose boundaries no page opened gives; the fortified town of Pondichéry is razed (1761) and rebuilt more than once.
Fixed enclaves from the 1816 restoration (Chandernagore 'a 3 sq mi (7.8 km2) enclave', Chandannagar page), surveyed as the 'five establishments'; the 1947 lodges are too small to draw.

notes:
Written by sa-06-b on 2026-10-25 from five pages (budget 5 for 9 shapes).

CLIOPATRIA SHAPE. All nine Cliopatria shapes are wrong as French India (verdict wrong; corrections give the five Indian establishments). Cell analysis with the gazetteer: the Name lumps French holdings across the Indian Ocean basin under French India: Réunion (9 cells in every shape except 1815-1819), Mauritius (5 cells, 1721-1814), Madagascar (33 cells, 1677-1720), the Comoros (2 cells, 1677-1845, and alone in 1815-1819), Akaroa/Banks Peninsula in New Zealand (2 cells, 1840-1845) and only 1-4 Indian cells (Pondichéry from 1677, Chandernagore from 1673, Yanam and Mahé from 1727; Karikal never). The pages opened do not list the Indian Ocean holdings (the French India page does not mention Mauritius, Réunion or the Mascarenes; the French East India Company page dates no territory). They need their own dossiers: see counterparts_needing_dossiers in the report (Île Bourbon/Réunion, Isle de France/Mauritius, French Madagascar, Akaroa). Cliopatria 'Mauritius' is the 1969-2024 state and cannot hold them.

KEYFRAME CONVENTION. A keyframe correction is the French holding at the start of its span; the ledger's gains and occupations add or hatch land inside the span (Chandernagore enters the 1677 span in 1692; Yanam and Mahé enter the 1721 span in 1723 and 1725; Karikal enters the 1727 span in 1739).

FAMILY/TYPE. type colony, family france (a dependency of the French state; the Cliopatria relations make it a member of the Kingdom of France umbrella 1673-1814 and of the republic, directory, consulate and empire umbrellas 1791-1814).

DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN PAGES. (1) Chandernagore: French India says 'established in 1692, with the permission of Nawab Shaista Khan'; Chandannagar says a factory in 1688 (40,000 coins to the Mughal subahdar), the name 'Chandernagor' in a letter of 1696, infobox 1696, Fort d'Orléans 1696-97. The ledger uses 1692. (2) Ryswick: 'regained the town in 1699 through the Treaty of Ryswick, signed on 20 September 1697'. (3) Chandernagore's transfer: French India and Chandannagar both give 2 May 1950; Chandannagar adds formal cession 2 Feb 1951 and de jure 9 June 1952 (its infobox calls 1951 'de facto'); merger with West Bengal 2 October 1954. (4) The page's 510 km2 is attributed to 1936 in the infobox and to 1950 in the text.

NOT SETTLED (page silent). The seller or ruler for Yanam (1723), Mahé (1725) and Karikal (1739): the ledger counterpart is 'unnamed local ruler (page silent)'. Whether the British also held Karikal, Mahé and Yanam in each occupation (the pages date only Pondichéry and Chandernagore). Dupleix's and Bussy's grants of 1749-1754 and any Northern Circars cession: the Carnatic Wars page does not mention them (a gap-filler should open 'Joseph François Dupleix' and 'Northern Circars'). The 1672 loss of Fort Saint Thomas and the 1668 Surat / 1669 Masulipatam factories (lost by 1720): not drawn. The lodges at Machilipatnam, Kozhikode and Surat (ceded 6 October 1947): too small for the grid, not drawn. The Cliopatria French shapes for the Kingdom of France, Republic, Directory, Consulate and Empire are the metropole dossiers of eu-20.

COUNTERPARTS. British East India Company has no dossier; counterparts use british-colonial-empire (to 1756) and british-empire (from 1757) as the Cliopatria rows that touch French India. dutch-east-india-company is the VOC dossier of another group. republic-of-india is written by another part of sa-06.

SMALL FEATURES. The enclaves (Chandernagore 16 km2 in the infobox, the four southern enclaves about 490 km2 together) are one to three res-5 cells each; region radii of 12-15 km were chosen to hit the cell; Chandernagore, Karaikal, Mahé and Yanam are not in places.jsonl (coordinates used; see report gazetteer_names_needed). Native names 'Inde française' and 'Établissements français dans l'Inde' are the French forms and were not read on a page.
